New executable defect: `.joe-janitor/rp06-failure-checkpoint-probe.py` injected one non-systemic ordinary Pass-1 criterion failure, then reran identical material with a healthy runner. comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RP-03 Jira Cloud/DC failure research update (2026-08-17)

Durable local brief: `.joe-janitor/rp03-jira-failure-taxonomy.md`; executable probes: `.joe-janitor/rp03-jira-dc-hidden-retry-probe.py` and `.joe-janitor/rp03-rate-limit-scope-probe.py`. No production or tracked file changed.

Recommended decision order is `classify -> determine replay safety -> retry/defer/re-observe -> one terminal operation outcome -> scoped finite-pass fuse`. Attempts never feed the fuse. Add `commit_unknown` for writes whose response was lost after Jira may have committed; create/comment/link/transition/update/delete must re-observe/dedupe before replay. A definitive Jira 429 is a rejected request and may be retried after the provider delay, unlike a connection loss with no response.

Failure scopes are now explicit. Ticket/operation: validation 400/422, isolated permission 403/concealed 404, 409/412 metadata/workflow conflict, payload/URI limit, moved/deleted issue handling, per-issue Cloud 429. Endpoint family: Cloud burst 429 and request-shape/unsupported-route defects. Write class: confirmed maintenance/read-only mode. Provider/pass: 401, CAPTCHA, failed authenticated principal/project preflight, invalid base URL/context/redirect, TLS/config failure, Cloud global/tenant quota defer, DC principal limiter defer. Snapshot/pass: partial/stalled/duplicated/contradictory pagination; incomplete data never becomes absence or advances lifecycle. Unknown Cloud 429 starts at method+endpoint family, not provider-wide. Provider outage inference requires terminal failures across >=2 tickets and >=2 independent endpoint families plus a hard per-pass cap; exact thresholds remain to calibrate.

Auto-heal paths include immutable-ID re-key, direct-read/index-lag corroboration (Cloud `reconcileIssues` where applicable), refresh/replan on 409/412 or metadata drift, smaller pages/POST for 413/414 without truncation, and desired-state observation after ambiguous writes. Permanent/configuration paths do not retry: TLS, CAPTCHA, invalid canonical URL/context, unsupported endpoint, repeated validation/permission/capability failure. Reads retry transient connect/reset/408/429/5xx with jitter; positive `Retry-After` is a lower bound and becomes `retry_not_before` when longer than the inline budget.

Direct factory verification found that Rebar calls `jira.JIRA` without `max_retries`, `timeout`, or `get_server_info`; locked jira 3.10.5 defaults to 3 internal retries, no timeout, and constructor `serverInfo` I/O. The local HTTP probe measured 4 hidden POSTs for one persistent create 429, 4 for create 503, 12 GETs for one paged-read 429 through both layers, and 12 lower-level create attempts on disconnect. Existing fake-client tests cannot observe this. Recommendation: singular retry ownership: DC `max_retries=0`, explicit connect/read timeouts, explicit bounded startup validation, and coordinator-owned retry/re-observation.

The scope probe found raw Cloud HTTP preserves `Retry-After` and `RateLimit-Reason`, but current DC `JIRAError -> BackendHTTPError` translation drops both; ACLI preserves a text delay but has no structured reason. Current common/DC/ACLI paths cap positive `Retry-After` at 60 seconds and retry early, contrary to Atlassian lower-bound guidance and pycontribs user report #1805. This is an explicit behavior correction, not parity.

Research grounds the taxonomy in Atlassian Cloud/DC docs and user reports from active pycontribs/jira: Cloud missing DC rate headers (#1463), CloudFront GET-body 403 (#1945), DC Retry-After zero/early-repeat (#1805), DC chunked/JSON failures (#1486/#1504), DC auth-losing redirect (#1196), CAPTCHA (#733), TLS retry (#966), link permission ambiguity (#1296), and transition drift (#740). Maintained OSS comparison: GitLab uses delayed bounded Jira retries; Sentry isolates by external issue and halts typed auth/config failures; controller-runtime requeues per object; Crossplane records create uncertainty and re-observes before proceeding.

Highest-leverage decision remaining before exact retry/fuse calibration: approve singular retry ownership, `commit_unknown`, authoritative Jira rate scopes, and the scoped finite-pass fuse foundation described above.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RP-03 retry ownership approved (2026-08-17).

The maintainer approved a two-level pattern suitable for future GitHub Issues, Linear, and other tracker adapters without adding those adapters to RP-03 scope. Concrete adapters own the only physical request-replay loop, request/subprocess timeouts and cleanup, native SDK retry configuration, provider error/header decoding, and physical-attempt evidence. The backend-neutral reconciler owns operation intent/postconditions, `commit_unknown`, write-ahead/lifecycle recovery, re-observation and re-planning, dependency deferral, long-delay scheduling, the scoped finite-pass fuse, and exact ticket/pass outcomes. `jira_family` may contain only pure Cloud/DC-shared classification/value behavior; it owns no retry loop, sleep, budget, clock, counter, or fuse.

Physical replay uses a two-key authorization rule: the core must declare the logical operation/postcondition replayable, and the concrete adapter must prove its exact request was not applied, provider-idempotent, or freshly/deterministically deduplicated. Either proof missing yields `commit_unknown` for core re-observation. Compound adapter methods are not one replay unit; late-leg failure preserves confirmed earlier effects and triggers re-observation rather than repeating the whole method. Configurable SDK retries are disabled (`jira.JIRA(max_retries=0)`); opaque CLI-native retries are never multiplied by an outer Rebar write retry. Physical attempts and logical operations are separate accounting dimensions.

The approved addendum is saved in `.joe-janitor/rp03-jira-failure-taxonomy.md` and `.joe-janitor/rp03-outbound-lifecycle-research.md`. This work did not touch the in-flight RP-04 epic, stories, worktree, or implementation state. Next RP-03 decision: calibrate inline physical retry/defer budgets and finite-pass fuse thresholds.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: RP-03 retry-budget calibration research (2026-08-17; proposal pending maintainer decision). Atlassian Cloud guidance uses bounded exponential backoff with jitter, an example two-second base/four retries/30-second delay ceiling, idempotency gating, and can return very long Retry-After values. Maintained GitLab Jira Connect uses three entity-worker retries; Sentry uses five isolated per-external-issue task retries; controller-runtime and Crossplane favor delayed per-object requeue/re-observation over holding a finite pass open. Current Rebar visible policies cluster at 3 total attempts with 6-7 seconds fallback sleep, while hidden DC SDK layering was experimentally shown to multiply calls to 12 or 16. ADR 0087s 60-second LLM wait cap and ADR 0084s Jira cap cannot be reused because positive Jira Retry-After is an authoritative lower bound. Recommended default: 3 physical attempts total and 15 seconds cumulative sleep per logical operation; nonzero jittered 1/2-second fallback windows; defer with retry_not_before whenever the provider delay plus one request timeout does not fit the shared allowance/deadline. Permit at most one immediate core observe-and-replan cycle for commit_unknown/conflict/drift, sharing rather than resetting that budget. Full notes: .joe-janitor/rp03-jira-failure-taxonomy.md. No production/tracked files or RP-04 state changed.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: RP-03 retry-envelope parallel validation complete (2026-08-17); full note: .joe-janitor/rp03-retry-envelope-validation.md. No workflow was dispatched, no tracked/production file changed, and RP-04 was untouched. Historical Actions: 16 live Jira Cloud jobs from Aug 5-17 all passed (17 tests/job, 64.34-129.55s, median about 84.3s) with no logged Jira 429/5xx, Retry-After, or transport timeout. The matching 16 DC jobs were 5 pass/11 fail; failures were semantic/state/capability or local Git defects, not transient Jira transport. Run 31879125045 job 94999114642 passed 73 tests in 4444.49s after 99 Jira readiness probes; readiness/provisioning is a separate lifecycle protocol and must not consume the operation retry budget. No sampled outcome needed a fourth Jira call or more than 15s inline sleep, but this is weak negative evidence because current logs omit physical-attempt telemetry and silent SDK/ACLI retries. Required observability is now explicit: logical operation/postcondition, physical count, delay source/value, remaining call/sleep/deadline budgets, retry_not_before, scope, and terminal outcome. OSS comparison found no exact numeric consensus: defaults range from one call to 11 depending on write/controller/read-only workload. Consensus is finite retries, Retry-After/reset as a lower bound, exponential backoff+jitter without an authoritative delay, separation of physical replay from delayed logical/job retry, and deferral of long waits. Jira examples: pycontribs defaults to 4 hidden calls; atlassian-python-api default rate handling is 2 calls; GitLab sends foreground Jira requests once then retries a worker at 30s/5m/30m; Sentry separates foreground translation from 5 background retries; Airbyte uses 11 calls for GET-only ingestion; Mattermost/go-jira sends once. GitHub Octokit defaults to 4 total calls and 14s cumulative sleep; python-gitlab is more lenient for 429; Linear leaves retry to callers. Recommendation refined to maximum 3 total physical invocations across one atomic logical postcondition, 15s cumulative sleep, 2s then 4s fallback with nonnegative jitter, authoritative delay as lower bound with retry_not_before deferral, and one observe/replan cycle sharing the same budgets. Atomic means compound ticket updates are decomposed and never replayed wholesale. Current delta: generic 4-call/core wrapping is removed; Cloud nested worst-case 12 and DC measured 4/12/theoretical 16 fall to 3; ACLI usually remains at 3 but stops blind permanent/ambiguous replay; 60s Retry-After capping is intentionally reversed; DC SDK retries are disabled; typed deferral/scope replaces exception-class-dependent blast radius. Preserved: auth/TLS/permanent-4xx fast abort, ACLI reaping and write-timeout protection, 404 isolation, write-ahead/index-lag/keyless recovery, single-send operations without deterministic identity, exact partial success, and no fictional rollback. Envelope is pending maintainer approval.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: RP-03 decision approved: maximum 3 physical wire/subprocess invocations across one atomic logical desired postcondition; maximum 15 seconds cumulative inline sleep; approximately 2s then 4s exponential fallback with nonnegative jitter; authoritative Retry-After/reset is a lower bound and produces retry_not_before deferral when it cannot fit; at most one observe/replan cycle shares the same call, sleep, and deadline budgets. Compound ticket updates are decomposed into atomic operations and never replayed wholesale. Provisioning/readiness polling stays outside this envelope. Structured physical/logical attempt telemetry is required because historical Actions logs cannot reveal silent SDK/ACLI retries. Approval and validation are recorded in .joe-janitor/rp03-retry-envelope-validation.md and rp03-jira-failure-taxonomy.md. No tracked files or RP-04 state changed.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: RP-03 finite-pass fuse threshold research (pending maintainer decision). Correction: an absolute five-failures-per-pass cap is unsafe for large healthy batches because five isolated failures among hundreds of successes would falsely open the provider. Maintained controllers usually requeue per entity; established circuit-breaker mechanics instead combine consecutive failures with sliding-window density. Envoy defaults to five consecutive raw 5xx responses; Resilience4j uses a 50% failure-rate threshold over a configurable window/minimum. Because one Rebar exhausted logical outcome already represents up to three physical calls, recommendation is: inferred endpoint-family scope opens after 3 consecutive exhausted provider-suspect logical outcomes across at least 2 tickets, or 5 exhausted among the latest 10 eligible outcomes after the window fills, across at least 2 tickets. Provider scope uses the same 3-consecutive or 5-of-10 thresholds but additionally requires at least 2 independent endpoint families. A matching success resets only the consecutive counter and remains in the rolling window; isolated old failures age out. Count only exhausted timeout/connect/unknown-429/5xx outcomes and actual provider successes; exclude permanent 4xx, validation, conflict, per-issue throttling, local deferral, and skipped calls. Authoritative auth/config/TLS/global/burst/per-issue/DC-rate signals keep their already-approved immediate scopes. Continuous outage therefore stops after at most 9 physical calls/45s retry sleep; alternating failure/success opens at 50% after 10 eligible operations. Fuse state is pass-local; retry_not_before carries deferral. Detailed note: .joe-janitor/rp03-jira-failure-taxonomy.md. No tracked files or RP-04 state changed.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RP-03 finite-pass fuse decision APPROVED (2026-08-17). Retain only the scoped three-consecutive arm; remove the rolling five-of-ten arm. Endpoint-family scope opens after 3 consecutive exhausted eligible logical outcomes across at least 2 tickets. Provider scope uses the same threshold and additionally requires at least 2 independent endpoint families. A matching successful logical outcome resets the consecutive counter. Physical attempts, recovered fallbacks, permanent ticket failures, and opaque unclassified diagnostics do not count. Authoritative auth/configuration/quota/rate-limit/per-issue signals retain their direct scopes.

Rationale: three exhausted logical outcomes can represent up to nine physical provider calls under the approved envelope, while the five-of-ten arm has neither maintained-Jira precedent nor historical Rebar calibration and could discard useful progress from an alternating success/failure batch. Current Rebar often aborts earlier based on exception representation, so the approved normalized fuse is more permissive and consistent.

Historical evidence status: the completed 1,200-run replay slice produced zero approved-fuse openings and zero premature stops; targeted incidents confirm that healed warnings, ticket-local 404s, opaque ACLI errors, and authoritative credential failures must not feed inferred outage state. Full replay of all 415 failed runs and remaining successful slices remains evidence-completion work, not an unresolved design decision. Local record updated: `.joe-janitor/rp03-fuse-history-validation.md`. No tracked or production file changed; RP-04 remains untouched.

comments.body:
RP-05 design finalized and explicitly approved against origin/main 3b34d8b449ae4b56a5da8fb434aa75df7194b0c4 (2026-08-18).

Approved end state: one stdlib-only immutable lazy command registry; every stable verb remains discoverable; every visible top-level command has canonical package-data help; overview/help/alias/unknown routing occurs before RP-04 operation-snapshot composition, config materialization, store mount, handler resolution, and optional imports. Exact aliases reuse canonical help; compatibility shims retain alias-specific help naming the replacement; hidden bridge-status resolves explicit help but remains undiscoverable; purge-bridge remains unknown. Nested parsing stays handler-owned. Semantic capabilities map to packaging extras and one of error/unavailable/abstain/fallback, but enforcement occurs only after the selected mode/backend is known and domain components retain their result shapes.

Implementation defaults accepted with the design: frozen dataclasses/typed enums; exact aliases embedded in routes (no alias chains); pure runtime validation for duplicate spellings, policy contradictions, unknown capability names, help-resource census, and retired-token collisions; full-extra CI—not normal startup—resolves every module:function handler/selector; compatibility exports are derived from the registry during expand/contract migration; docs/reference and discovery checks enumerate the registry; no plugin discovery, second argument parser, DI container, or middleware framework.

Adversarial critique: validating handler strings during ordinary startup would defeat lazy imports, so reference resolution is isolated to the full-extra contract lane; capability policy is descriptive/shared-error infrastructure only, so metrics/grounding/rich-text fallbacks remain domain-owned; the 714-line current facade requires a dedicated registry module under the 800-line cap. Focused current-main baseline: 69 passed, 11 skipped; CLI-reference generation current; no heavy optional modules imported by rebar._cli.

Dependency: implementation is blocked on RP-04 contract completion (vibrant-legal-hind, especially junior-lepidolite-boa) because its centralized operation-composition cutover owns overlapping src/rebar seams. comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RP-05 parser/help refinement approved and researched against current `origin/main` (`3b34d8b449ae4b56a5da8fb434aa75df7194b0c4`). Current `docs/cli-reference.md` is generated, but its syntax authority is not: `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` embeds 54 hand-maintained package-help files plus a curated 22-command intercept table and regex-parses the facade. It detects census drift, not parser/help drift. Source census found reusable argparse construction in only a minority of command families (`_bridge_commands`, `_jira_onboard`, `_llm_commands`, `_llm_eval_commands`, `_workflow_commands`, and six standalone command modules); most core ticket/store handlers still parse argv imperatively.

Approved exact mechanism: every command grammar moves to a side-effect-free stdlib argparse factory; runtime handlers and the help generator call that same factory. Existing argparse builders are extracted. Imperative parsers migrate with accepted/rejected argv, double-dash handling, diagnostics, streams, and exit codes pinned by production-path compatibility tests. A narrow shared `ArgumentParser` subclass/formatter may preserve Rebar diagnostics; there is no docs-only parser, source-regex grammar, Click dependency, or second parser. Parser factories live in lean modules and accept a deterministic `prog`; generation alone resolves all factory refs, uses fixed formatting, and commits package-help/overview bytes. Runtime help remains a package-data read before RP-04 snapshot/config/mount/handler/optional imports.

Aliases do not duplicate grammar: exact aliases reuse canonical artifacts; bridge compatibility forms compose the same argument-definition helpers with alias-specific `prog` and replacement epilog; `jira-onboard` keeps its historical spelling; hidden `bridge-status` stays explicitly helpable but undiscoverable; `purge-bridge` stays unknown. The top-level lexical selector only identifies the command and first-token help/unknown forms, so it is routing rather than a competing argument grammar. Curated explanations/examples may remain editorial, but syntax/option tables must be generated or mechanically cross-checked.

Prior art inspected at current upstream heads supports the same-source model: CPython argparse uses the same parser actions for `parse_args()` and `format_help()`; Django `BaseCommand.create_parser()` feeds both `print_help()` and `run_from_argv()`; Click derives parsing/help from one parameter graph; Cobra Markdown docs walk the execution command tree. Sources: https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Lib/argparse.py ; https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/core/management/base.py ; https://github.com/pallets/click/blob/main/src/click/core.py ; https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/main/doc/md_docs.go .

Migration is expand/contract by command family: each factory lands with its handler switched to it and behavioral parity tests. Generated artifacts become authoritative only when the complete registry/parser census passes, preventing a shipped docs-only grammar. Code and generated artifacts roll back together; no persisted data changes. Local detail appended to `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.joe-janitor/rp05-cli-registry-research.md`. No production or tracked file changed.
